h1: Lake Louise ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Lake Louise sits at 1,538 metres in Banff National Park, and the ski resort above it spreads across three mountains and five separate faces - over 4,200 acres, 170 named runs and 991 metres of vertical, served by 13 lifts. A quarter of it is graded beginner and 45 per cent intermediate, and the longest run goes on for eight kilometres. The season is planned from 6 November 2026 to 2 May 2027.

stayOverview: The hamlet sits by the Bow River with the ski resort across the valley and the lake itself four kilometres up the hill. Banff is 57 kilometres down the Trans-Canada Highway and has far more beds.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. Lake Louise is small and inside a national park, so rooms are limited; Banff is the fallback.
rentalCars: Lake Louise is on the Trans-Canada Highway, about two hours west of Calgary and 57 kilometres from Banff.

history.label: 1870s
history.text: During the 1870s, construction of the Canadian Pacific Railway (CPR) began, with the route going through Bow Valley.
A Nakoda guide took CPR workman Tom Wilson to the site in 1882, and Wilson named it 'Emerald Lake'.
Lake Louise was added to Rocky Mountains Park in 1892, and has subsequently become an international tourist destination, made more accessible by its location near the Trans-Canada Highway.
1890 CPR station was replaced in 1910, but continued to be used by the railway company for other purposes until it was donated to Heritage Park Historical Village, Calgary, in 1976.
The 1910 station was declared a heritage railway station by the federal government in 1991, having been well-preserved and operating today as a restaurant.

history.label: Growth
history.text: In the language of the Nakoda people, Lake Louise is called Ho-run-num-nay, meaning "lake of the little fishes".

history.label: Civic role
history.text: The community was later called 'Holt City', and then 'Laggan', before being renamed Lake Louise.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The depot was moved to the park, where it was restored in the style of the era when the village was called Laggan.
